source.title: On the Power and Limitations of Random Features for Understanding Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a theoretical result about SGD training from random initialization, but it does not test any listed version’s specific datasets, model conditions, or outcomes. Its polynomial-learning result is related evidence for gradient-based trainability and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own theorem concerns expected hinge loss relative to a bounded-degree polynomial predictor. Its random-feature approximation limitations are theoretical results about a different operation, not tests of the listed training-error versions. CIFAR, ImageNet, local-minimum frequency, depth, initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability, and batch-normalization results appear only as background or citations.
record.test_reason: The paper proves polynomial-learning guarantees and random-feature approximation lower bounds. Neither measures any listed version's specified effect. References to memorization, extra width and Xavier initialization do not test those versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors prove a restricted SGD guarantee for learning bounded-degree polynomials and argue that random-feature explanations cannot fully explain neural-network learnability. Their negative results concern fixed-feature approximation, rather than failure of fully trained neural networks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proves a theoretical SGD guarantee for polynomial learning and theoretical inapproximability results for random features; it does not reproduce the benchmark training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The polynomial-learning guarantee depends on the activation’s Taylor coefficients, polynomial degree and coefficient bounds, network width, learning rate, and iteration count, as specified in Theorem 3.1.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 3.1 guarantees that some SGD iterate competes with a bounded-degree polynomial predictor in expected hinge loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated activation, width, initialization and SGD assumptions, expected hinge loss reaches the polynomial predictor's loss plus ε.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.1–4.2 establish approximation lower bounds for fixed random features targeting a single ReLU neuron under Gaussian inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated feature-norm and target assumptions, sufficiently accurate approximation requires an exponentially large product of feature count and maximum output-weight magnitude.

record.problems: The paper’s own training result is a theoretical expected-loss bound under restrictive assumptions; it does not report benchmark classification training errors or compare the initialization, depth, width, normalization, or learning-rate conditions in the listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows: cited benchmark and optimization findings are prior work, not results of this paper.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and recipe-dependent failures.
Spurious-minimum frequency in ReLU teacher-student training and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and the specified alternative initialization recipes.
Comparative training speed or trainable depth under activation-matched, orthogonal and Gaussian initializations.
Recovery, curvature dynamics and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Remark 3.1 applies the polynomial guarantee to empirical loss on a finite sample, but does not establish the benchmark convolutional-network claim in V1. Using Xavier initialization alone does not test V4.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and the specified optimizer recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU minima, joint teacher/student width, and extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual network training error, depth, normalization, and the cited alternative initialization or Fixup recipes.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep convolutional training.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, loss recovery, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch-normalization speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer feed-forward neural network N(W, U, x)
rows.size_stated: r neurons, with r satisfying Theorem 3.1’s lower bound
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 3.1 bounds expected SGD loss relative to a bounded-degree polynomial predictor under the stated activation and data assumptions.

conditions.value: any distribution over labeled (x, y) with ||x|| ≤ 1 and y ∈ {−1, +1}
analytic, L-Lipschitz, with the Taylor-coefficient conditions in Theorem 3.1
polynomial of degree at most k with coefficients bounded by α, subject to the stated Taylor-series condition

rows.measure: Expected loss along SGD relative to the polynomial predictor’s loss
rows.value: E[LD(Wt, Ut)] ≤ LD(P(x)) + ε for some t ∈ [T]
rows.uncertainty: With probability > 1 − δ over initialization; expectation over SGD examples
rows.note: The theorem concerns hinge loss and polynomial targets, not zero training classification error on the benchmarks in the claim versions. It is therefore not assigned to a listed version.
rows.check: The theorem establishes the recorded relative hinge-loss guarantee, but this measure cannot establish any listed version's effect. The learning rate is ε/(8r), not ε/(8r²); the superscript following the denominator in the extracted text belongs to the next expression.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
